clues: This city in Sweden sits on an inlet of the Baltic Sea. People count it as a true coastal place.
Warm summers meet winters that hover near freezing point here. Its snow cover comes and goes in the cold months.
Before twelve thirty, old records used a different name for this town. Then its new name showed up on coins that year.
For thousands of years, the land under downtown was a chain of islands. Its hills were islands, and its flat land was sea floor.
This city is home to Stockholm Skavsta Airport. The airport sits just a short trip from the city centre.
